# read_B: pp. 102–104 (images n103–n105), plus the seam line 101.5 (n102), read from the images

## Lines and layout
- p. 101 (n102), seam only: skew about +1.6°, read from a straightened copy.
- p. 102 (n103) has five lines. It is a leaf back with no ornament. Skew is about −1.4°, so I read it straightened.
- p. 103 (n104) has five lines. It is a leaf front. It opens with the horizontal swirl, then `༔`, a wide blank, and `༔`, written `༄༅༔ ༔` as in 009/010. The leaf number is in the left margin. Skew is about +2.0°, so I read it straightened.
- p. 104 (n105) has five lines. It is a leaf back with no ornament. Skew is about −1.8°, so I read it straightened.
- In all I read 15 print lines, plus the seam line 101.5.

**Seam with A (101.5, log only).** I read it as `…ཚོགས་པ་རང་གི་ཀླད་པའི་ནང་ནས་ཐོན་ནས་རང་ལ་འཆར་དུ་འོང་ངོ༔ ཡང་ངོ་སྤྲད་པ་ནི༔ ཚེ་འདས་ཀྱི་མིང་ནས་བོས་ལ་འདི་སྐད་དོ༔ ཀྱེ་རིགས`.
- `རིགས` at the frame has no tsheg, and p. 102 opens `ཀྱི་བུ༔`.
- So the seam reads `…ཀྱེ་རིགས|ཀྱི་བུ༔ མ་ཡེངས་པར་ཉོན་ཅིག༔`, which is clean apart from the missing tsheg (fix below).
- This is the twelfth-day introduction to the eight Gaurīs (witness: `…ཡང་ངོ་སྤྲད་པ་ནི༔ ཚེ་འདས་ཀྱི་མིང་ནས་བོས་ལ་འདི་སྐད་དོ༔ ཀྱེ་རིགས་ཀྱི་བུ་མ་ཡེངས་པར་ཉོན་ཅིག༔ …`). In the print, the shorter list `ཀོ་རཱི་མ་མོ་བརྒྱད་ཐོན་ནས…མ་འཇིགས་ཤིག` seems not to come between `ཉོན་ཅིག༔` and `རང་གི་ཀླད་པའི་ཤར་ནས`. See the sense differences.

**Seam with C (104.5).** p. 104 ends `…རང་གི་ཀླད་པའི་ནང་ནས་`, with a tsheg. p. 105 should go on with `ཐོན་ནས…`.

## Method
- I found the line bands from row profiles. Skew was found by maximising row-profile variance, and each page was read from a rotated copy.
- Each line was cropped in 4–5 overlapping segments at ×3–×4.
- Doubtful stacks were cropped at ×6–×14 (LANCZOS).
- I checked line-end tshegs at ×8–×12.
- Mid-line tshegs are often fused to the headline. Where the image cannot decide, I followed normal syllable division.

## Other doubtful points (no [?] set)
- **104.3 `ཀ་ཀ་མུ་ཁ`.** The witness has `ཀང་ཀ་མུ་ཀ`. I see no ང or anusvāra on the first ཀ. Kept, note only.
- **104.3 `ཁ་ཁ་མུ་ཁ`.** There is a slanted stroke (like `/`) after `ནས` and before the first ཁ. I take it as a stray mark, not a shad, and do not write it. The second ཁ is cramped.
- **104.1 `རོ་ཁ་ཁྱེ་ནས`.** The witness has `རོ་ཁར་ཁྱེར་ནས`. I see no ར on either syllable at ×10. Written as seen; probably a misprint or cramped cutting. Kept, note only.
- **104.4/104.5 `རལ་གྲི`.** A dot sits between ར and ལ in both places. I take it as a fleck, not a tsheg.
- **103.5 `ཞིང་` / 104.1 `སྤུ`**: the join is clean.

## Where this print differs in sense from the other recension (print followed)
- **102.1:** the print has `རང་གི་ཀླད་པའི་ཤར་ནས་གོའུ་རི་མ་དཀར་མོ` right after "listen without distraction". The witness first has `རང་གི་ཀླད་པའི་ནང་ནས་ཀོ་རཱི་མ་མོ་བརྒྱད་ཐོན་ནས…འོང་ངོ༔ དེ་ལ་མ་འཇིགས་ཤིག༔`. The print lacks that general announcement (unless A's 101.5 has it earlier; it does not in my reading of 101.5).
- **102.1–2:** `བྷན་དྷ་དམར་གྱི་བཀང་ཐོགས་ནས` ("holding [a skull-cup] filled with blood") for the witness `…བཀང་བ་བསྣམས་ནས`. The sense is the same.
- **102.2:** the print has `ཙོའུ་རི་མ` (with མ) and `ཕྲ་མོ་དམར་མོ`, where the witness has `ཕྲ་མེན་དམར་མོ` (Pramohā). See the misprints.
- **102.3:** Vetālī holds "a vajra **and** a skull-cup filled with blood", as in the witness.
- **102.4:** Ghasmarī holds the skull-cup in the **left hand** (`གཡོན་ན`), as in the witness.
- **102.5:** for Ghasmarī the print has `གཡས་པའི་རྡོ་རྗེས་དཀྲུགས་ཅིང་ཉམས་པའི་ཆུ་ལ་གྲིས་ཞལ་དུ་གསོལ་བ`. The words `ཉམས[?]་པའི་ཆུ[?]་ལ་གྲིས` are not in the witness, and I cannot construe them.
- **102.5–103.1:** Caṇḍālī: the print has "**loading** head and body on her shoulder" (`མགོ་ལུས་ཕྲག་པ་བཀལ་ཏེ`), where the witness has "**tearing apart** head and body" (`མགོ་ལུས་ཕྲལ་བ`).
- **103.1–2:** Śmaśānī: the print has `སྨེ་ཤ་ནི་མཐིང་ནག་མགོ་ལུས་ཕྲལ་ནས་ཟ་བ`. It lacks `ཞིང་གི` ("of a corpse").
- **103.2:** the print has `ཐོན་ནས་འཆར་དུ་འོང་ངོ`. It lacks `རང་ལ`, and it has `ཡབ་ལྔ་ལ་བསྐོར`.
- **103.3:** the print omits `མ་ཡེངས་པར་ཉོན་ཅིག` after `ཀྱེ་རིགས་ཀྱི་བུ༔` (as at 96.5 and 93.3), and has `ཕྲ་མེན་མ་བརྒྱད`. The print **lacks `མུ་ཀ` in `སེང་ཧ་སྨུག་ནག`** (witness `སེང་ཧ་མུ་ཀ་སྨུག་ནག`). It may be haplography, `སེང་ཧ་[མུ་ཁ་]སྨུག`. Kept, note only.
- **103.4:** `ལག་གཉིས་བྲང་ཁར་བསྣོལ…རོ་ཐོགས་རལ་པ་བསིགས་པ`. The witness has `ཐོགས་ཏེ`; the sense is the same. The print has `སྟག་མགོ་མ`, and lacks `མཐུར་དུ` ("downward") for the crossed arms (104.5 `ལག་གཉིས་བསྣོལ་ནས`).
- **103.5:** Śṛgālamukhā is `ཝ་མགོ་ཅན` **without colour** (the witness has `ནག་མོ`). The print **lacks the razor here**: right hand `རྒྱུ་མ་བཟུང་ཞིང་` / 104.1 `སྤུ་གྲི་ཐོགས་ནས་གཡོན་པས་རྒྱུ་མ་ཟ་བ`. So the print has right hand intestines, then razor, then the left hand eating intestines. The witness has right hand razor and left hand intestines.
- **104.1:** `ལག་པ་གཉིས་ཀྱི་རོ་ཁ་ཁྱེ་ནས` / 104.2 `མིག་འབྲུ་ཚུགས་སུ་བལྟ་བ`. The sense is the same.
- **104.2:** Gṛdhramukhā carries the great corpse `ཕྲག་ལ་ཁུར་ནས`, as in the witness.
- **104.3–4:** Kākamukhā has `གཡོན་དུ་བྷནྡྷ་ཐོགས་ནས༔ གཡས་པས་རལ་གྲི་ཐོགས་ཏེ`, as in the witness. The sense is the same.
- **104.4–5: Ulūkamukhā** has `གཡས་སུ་རྡོ་རྗེ་ཐོགས་ཤིང་གཡོན་དུ་རལ་གྲི་བསྣམས་ཤིང་ཤ་ཟ་བ` ("in the left a sword, eating flesh"). The witness has `གཡོན་པས་དུང་ཁྲག་འཐུང་བ` ("drinking blood from a conch with the left"). **This is a real difference.**
- **104.5:** the summary has `ཡུལ་གྱི་ཕྲ་མེན་མ་བརྒྱད་པོ`, where the witness has `ཕྲ་མེན་བརྒྱད་པོ`.

## Fixes needed (`# fix:` lines)
```
# fix: ཀྱེ་རིགསཀྱི་བུ => ཀྱེ་རིགས་ཀྱི་བུ
# fix: འཆར་དུ་འོངངོ་༔ => འཆར་དུ་འོང་ངོ་༔
# fix: གཡོན་དུབྷནྡྷཐོགས་ནས => གཡོན་དུ་བྷནྡྷ་ཐོགས་ནས
```
- The first fix is the seam with A, and it applies to the joined source.
- If the editor judges the dot after 102.5 `ལུས` to be filler and not a tsheg, add the following (the ornament is stripped before fixes, as in 010):
  ```
  # fix: མགོ་ལུསཕྲག་པ => མགོ་ལུས་ཕྲག་པ
  ```
- No `པའཾ`, `ལཾ`, `ནམཁའ` or subscript-ས abbreviations occur on these pages.

## Suspected misprints (all kept, note only)
1. **102.2 `ཕྲ་མོ་དམར་མོ`** for `ཕྲ་མེན་དམར་མོ`. This is probably a misprint: Pramohā is `ཕྲ་མེན` in this text (103.3, 104.5). Moderate certainty. The fix would be `ཕྲ་མེན`, but the name could be the print's own form, so I propose no fix.
2. **102.5 `ཉམས་པའི་ཆུ་ལ་གྲིས`**: uncertain letters, and the sense is unclear. The editor should look.
3. **103.3 `སེང་ཧ་སྨུག`**, probably for `སེང་ཧ་མུ་ཁ་སྨུག` (haplography).
4. **104.1 `རོ་ཁ་ཁྱེ`** for `རོ་ཁར་ཁྱེར`; **104.4 `མཐིང་ན`** for `མཐིང་ནག`; **104.3 `ཀ་ཀ་མུ་ཁ`** for `ཀང་ཀ་མུ་ཁ`.
5. **`མུ་ཁ` for `མུ་ཀ` (-mukha) throughout.** This is the print's spelling, not a misprint. Kept.
